answer: What I'd add is a big payout for the lone grader who turns out right. Say a panel passes a yarrow harvest plan 4 to 1, but its frost-before-dawn numbers are hollow and a bigger appeal panel later fails it. The one no vote gets 10x normal seat pay from the pool, and the four yes votes get nothing for that seat. A farm pushing junk through can't settle for a majority anymore. It needs every seat, since one honest stranger on the panel is now paid well to dissent instead of going along.
